bank.q: Consider the following statements about the structure of the judicial crisis:
s: District and subordinate courts hold roughly 85 to 87% of total pendency.
Subordinate judicial vacancies stand at around 23%.
India has roughly 21 judges per million people against a benchmark of 50.
bank.e: All three are correct, and together they explain why reform attention keeps returning to the lowest tier.

bank.q: Match List I (case) with List II (holding):
pairs: 1. Prior permission of the Chief Justice is needed to investigate a judge
2. Articles 32 and 226 are part of the basic structure
4. The collegium system with primacy to the Chief Justice
bank.e: L. Chandra Kumar on entrenching review, Veeraswami on investigation, the Second Judges Case on the collegium, and the Fourth on the NJAC.

bank.q: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: No Indian judge has ever been removed by completed impeachment
Article 142 directions carry no precedential value
Delimitation orders are open to judicial review
Control over the subordinate judiciary vests in the High Court
bank.e: Articles 329, 243-O and 243-ZG expressly bar judicial interference with delimitation.

bank.as: Judicial independence and judicial accountability are described as mutually necessary rather than opposed.
bank.rs: Independence without accountability tends towards judicial supremacy, while accountability without independence tends towards political subordination.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the formulation constitutional morality demands.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about appointments:
s: The collegium system has no textual basis in the Constitution.
High Court vacancies stood at around 30% in mid-2026.
The All India Judicial Service requires a constitutional amendment to create.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Article 312 already empowers Parliament to create the service — no amendment is needed.

bank.q: Which pair correctly matches a power with the court that holds it?
o: Curative petitions — High Courts and the Supreme Court
Article 142 complete justice — the Supreme Court alone
Article 226 writs — the Supreme Court alone
Article 235 control of the district judiciary — the Supreme Court
bank.e: Article 142 belongs to the Supreme Court alone, as do Articles 131, 137 and 143. Article 226 belongs to High Courts and Article 235 gives them control over the district judiciary.

bank.q: All of the following are examples of judicial activism EXCEPT:
o: The Vishaka guidelines on workplace harassment
Suo motu cognisance of the migrant crisis
bank.e: The presumption of constitutionality is a component of judicial restraint, placing the burden on the challenger.

bank.q: Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
bank.e: S. P. Gupta (1981) → the Second Judges Case (1993) → L. Chandra Kumar (1997) → the NJAC judgment (2015).

bank.q: With reference to the Attorney General, consider the following:
s: The office may participate in parliamentary proceedings but not vote.
Its remuneration is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
Private practice is permitted, subject to not appearing against the Union.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Remuneration is fixed by the government and is not charged on the Consolidated Fund.

bank.as: Recent case law shows the Court increasingly using continuing supervision rather than one-off orders.
bank.rs: Matters such as the stray dogs case, Chambal sand mining and punitive demolitions were handled through multi-stage proceedings with escalating directions.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — continuing mandamus has become the default technique for institutional failure cases.
